title: City Life & Housing
subtitle: Describe your home, explore your neighbourhood and move house

lessons.title: Mon appartement
lessons.description: Describe the rooms and furniture of your home and say exactly where things are.

blocks.heading: Les pièces de la maison
blocks.body: A French home is described room by room: une pièce is a room in general, while la chambre is specifically a bedroom. Adverts count rooms without the kitchen and bathroom, so « un trois pièces » means a living room plus two bedrooms. Note that la salle de bains keeps an s on bains, and les toilettes are almost always plural.

examples.french: Mon appartement a trois pièces.
examples.english: My apartment has three rooms.

examples.french: La cuisine est petite mais claire.
examples.english: The kitchen is small but bright.

examples.french: Nous mangeons dans le salon.
examples.english: We eat in the living room.

examples.french: La salle de bains est au fond du couloir.
examples.english: The bathroom is at the end of the hallway.

examples.french: J'habite au troisième étage, sans ascenseur.
examples.english: I live on the third floor, with no elevator.

blocks.tip: In France the ground floor is le rez-de-chaussée, so « le premier étage » is what Americans call the second floor.

blocks.heading: Les meubles et l'équipement
blocks.body: Furniture words are very concrete and most are borrowed into English in some form. Un meuble is a single piece of furniture and des meubles is furniture in general. To say what a room contains, French uses il y a — the same form for singular and plural.

examples.french: Dans le salon, il y a un canapé et deux fauteuils.
examples.english: In the living room there is a sofa and two armchairs.

examples.french: Mon lit est très confortable.
examples.english: My bed is very comfortable.

examples.french: Je range mes vêtements dans l'armoire.
examples.english: I put my clothes away in the wardrobe.

examples.french: Il y a un grand tapis sous la table.
examples.english: There is a big rug under the table.

examples.french: Le frigo est vide, il faut faire les courses.
examples.english: The fridge is empty, we need to go shopping.

blocks.tip: Careful with faux amis: « une librairie » is a bookshop, and « un canapé » is a sofa — not a canopy.

blocks.heading: Simple prepositions: dans, sur, sous, devant, derrière, entre
blocks.body: These short prepositions go straight in front of the noun with its article — nothing changes. Dans means inside, sur means on a surface, sous means underneath, devant is in front of and derrière is behind. Entre needs two things, joined by et.

examples.french: Le livre est sur l'étagère.
examples.english: The book is on the shelf.

examples.french: Mes chaussures sont sous le lit.
examples.english: My shoes are under the bed.

examples.english: There is a rug in front of the door.

blocks.tip: Dans le salon = inside the living room; au salon (à + le) is also possible and sounds slightly more formal.

blocks.heading: Prepositions ending in de: watch the contraction
blocks.body: à côté de, en face de, près de, loin de and au-dessus de all end in de, and de contracts with the article: de + le = du, de + les = des. Before la and l' nothing changes. Getting this contraction right is what makes your description sound French.

blocks.tip: If you drop the noun, the de disappears too: « La pharmacie ? Elle est juste à côté. »

lessons.title: Dans mon quartier
lessons.description: Name the shops, services and public places around you and say where you are going.

blocks.heading: Les commerces du quartier
blocks.body: Most French shop names are built from the product plus the ending -erie: le pain gives la boulangerie, la viande gives la boucherie. The shopkeeper takes -er or -ère: le boulanger, la boulangère. These small shops are still part of daily life, even next to big supermarkets.

examples.french: J'achète une baguette à la boulangerie.
examples.english: I buy a baguette at the bakery.

examples.french: La boucherie ferme le lundi.
examples.english: The butcher's is closed on Mondays.

examples.french: Il y a une petite épicerie au coin de la rue.
examples.english: There is a small grocery shop on the corner of the street.

examples.french: Le samedi, on fait les courses au marché.
examples.english: On Saturdays we do the shopping at the market.

examples.french: Je vais chez le coiffeur cet après-midi.
examples.english: I'm going to the hairdresser's this afternoon.

blocks.tip: For a shop named after a person, French says chez: chez le boulanger, chez le médecin, chez le coiffeur.

blocks.heading: Les services et les lieux publics
blocks.body: Every French town centre has the same core services: la mairie for paperwork, la poste for letters, la banque for money and le commissariat for the police. Public places such as le parc, la bibliothèque and la piscine are usually municipal, so their names appear on street signs with the word municipal(e).

examples.french: Je dois passer à la poste avant midi.

examples.french: La mairie se trouve sur la place principale.

examples.french: L'arrêt de bus est juste devant la pharmacie.

blocks.tip: In small towns, ask « Où est le centre-ville ? » — everything useful is usually within a few streets.

sections.title: Grammar — aller à, venir de, aller chez

blocks.heading: Going to a place: à + article
blocks.body: To say where you are going, use aller à plus the place. The preposition à merges with the article: à + le = au, à + les = aux, while à la and à l' stay unchanged. The same forms are used with être to say where you are.

examples.french: Je vais à la boulangerie.
examples.english: I'm going to the bakery.

examples.french: Nous allons au marché ce matin.
examples.english: We're going to the market this morning.

examples.french: Elle va à l'école à pied.
examples.english: She walks to school.

examples.french: Ils vont aux magasins du centre.
examples.english: They're going to the shops in the centre.

examples.french: Tu es à la piscine ?
examples.english: Are you at the swimming pool?

examples.french: On se retrouve au parc à quatre heures.
examples.english: Let's meet at the park at four.

blocks.tip: Aller is irregular: je vais, tu vas, il/elle va, nous allons, vous allez, ils/elles vont.

blocks.heading: Coming from a place, and going to someone's: de and chez
blocks.body: Venir de means to come from, and de contracts the same way: de + le = du, de + les = des. When the destination is a person or a profession, French uses chez instead of à: chez le médecin, chez ma sœur, chez moi.

examples.french: Je viens de la pharmacie.
examples.english: I'm coming from the pharmacy.

examples.french: Il revient du supermarché.
examples.english: He's coming back from the supermarket.

examples.french: Elles rentrent des magasins.
examples.english: They're coming home from the shops.

examples.french: Je vais chez le coiffeur.
examples.english: I'm going to the hairdresser's.

examples.french: On dîne chez mes parents ce soir.
examples.english: We're having dinner at my parents' place tonight.

examples.french: Reste chez toi, il pleut.
examples.english: Stay at home, it's raining.

blocks.tip: Chez is never followed by an article: chez le médecin (a person) but à la pharmacie (a place).

passages.title: Samedi matin dans le quartier
passages.french:

D'abord, il va à la boulangerie pour acheter des croissants.
Ensuite, il traverse la place et fait les courses au marché.
Il aime bien parler avec les vendeurs de fruits et légumes.
Vers dix heures, il passe à la poste pour envoyer un colis à sa sœur.
Après, il s'arrête au café du coin et lit le journal.
La banque est fermée l'après-midi, alors il y va avant midi.
Enfin, il rentre chez lui les bras pleins de sacs.
Il adore son quartier : tout se fait à pied.

lessons.title: Déménager
lessons.description: Handle renting and moving house, and compare two homes with plus, moins and aussi.

blocks.heading: Chercher et louer un logement
blocks.body: Renting in France follows a fixed sequence: you read une annonce, you book une visite, then you sign le bail and pay la caution. Le loyer is the rent itself, and les charges (water, heating, building upkeep) may be included or not — adverts say charges comprises or hors charges. Un logement meublé comes with furniture; un logement vide does not.

examples.french: J'ai vu une annonce pour un studio meublé.
examples.english: I saw an ad for a furnished studio flat.

examples.french: La visite est prévue jeudi à dix-huit heures.
examples.english: The viewing is scheduled for Thursday at six p.m.

examples.french: Le loyer est de 700 euros, charges comprises.
examples.english: The rent is 700 euros, bills included.

examples.french: Il faut payer une caution d'un mois.
examples.english: You have to pay a deposit of one month's rent.

examples.french: Nous avons signé le bail hier après-midi.
examples.english: We signed the lease yesterday afternoon.

blocks.tip: Before you get the keys you do l'état des lieux, a written check of the flat's condition — take photos, it protects your deposit.

blocks.heading: Le jour du déménagement
blocks.body: Déménager means to move out, emménager means to move in, and s'installer means to settle in. The whole event is un déménagement. Note that these verbs take avoir in the passé composé: j'ai déménagé, nous avons emménagé.

examples.french: Nous déménageons le premier septembre.
examples.english: We are moving on the first of September.

examples.french: J'ai rempli vingt cartons en deux jours.
examples.english: I filled twenty boxes in two days.

examples.french: Ils ont loué un camion pour le déménagement.
examples.english: They rented a van for the move.

examples.french: Elle a emménagé dans un appartement plus grand.
examples.english: She moved into a bigger apartment.

examples.french: On s'installe petit à petit.
examples.english: We're settling in bit by bit.

blocks.tip: Déménager keeps an e before -ons: nous déménageons — the e keeps the g soft.

blocks.heading: plus / moins / aussi ... que
blocks.body: French makes comparisons with one simple frame: plus (more), moins (less) or aussi (as) before the adjective, then que before the second element. Unlike English, there is no -er ending: bigger is simply plus grand. The adjective still agrees with the first noun: plus grande, plus grands.

examples.french: Mon appartement est plus grand que le tien.
examples.english: My apartment is bigger than yours.

examples.french: Cette rue est moins bruyante que le boulevard.
examples.english: This street is less noisy than the boulevard.

examples.french: Le studio est aussi cher que le deux-pièces.
examples.english: The studio is as expensive as the one-bedroom flat.

examples.french: La cuisine est plus lumineuse que la chambre.
examples.english: The kitchen is brighter than the bedroom.

examples.french: Les loyers sont moins élevés en banlieue.
examples.english: Rents are lower in the suburbs.
examples.note: que + comparison can be left out when it is obvious

examples.french: Elle est aussi contente que moi.
examples.english: She is as happy as I am.
examples.note: after que use moi, toi, lui, elle

blocks.tip: The same frame works with adverbs and with nouns: il parle plus vite que moi; j'ai plus de place qu'avant (note plus DE + noun).

blocks.heading: Irregular: meilleur and mieux, plus the superlative
blocks.body: Plus bon does not exist — the adjective bon becomes meilleur, and the adverb bien becomes mieux. For the superlative (the most / the least), add the definite article in front: le plus, la plus, les plus. With an adjective that follows the noun, the article is repeated: le quartier le plus calme.

examples.french: Ce quartier est meilleur que l'autre.
examples.english: This neighbourhood is better than the other one.

examples.french: Je dors mieux depuis le déménagement.
examples.english: I sleep better since the move.

examples.french: C'est l'appartement le plus lumineux de l'immeuble.
examples.english: It's the brightest apartment in the building.

examples.french: C'est la solution la moins chère.
examples.english: It's the cheapest solution.

examples.french: Ce sont les quartiers les plus agréables de la ville.
examples.english: These are the most pleasant districts in the city.

examples.french: C'est la meilleure boulangerie du quartier.
examples.english: It's the best bakery in the neighbourhood.
examples.note: after a superlative, use de, not dans

blocks.tip: Meilleur describes a noun (un meilleur loyer), mieux describes an action (on vit mieux ici).

passages.title: Deux appartements, un choix difficile
passages.french:
Julie et Marc cherchent un logement depuis deux mois.
Ils ont visité deux appartements le même après-midi.
Le premier est dans le centre : il est lumineux mais assez cher.
Le loyer est de 900 euros, charges comprises.
Le deuxième est en banlieue, à côté d'un parc.
Il est plus grand et beaucoup moins cher : 650 euros.
Mais il est aussi plus loin du travail de Marc.
« Le centre est plus pratique », dit Marc.
« Oui, mais l'autre est plus calme et on dort mieux », répond Julie.
Finalement, ils choisissent la banlieue et signent le bail lundi.
passages.english:
Julie and Marc have been looking for a place for two months.
They visited two apartments the same afternoon.
The first is in the centre: it is bright but quite expensive.
The rent is 900 euros, bills included.
The second is in the suburbs, next to a park.
It is bigger and much cheaper: 650 euros.
But it is also further from Marc's work.
"The centre is more convenient," says Marc.
"Yes, but the other one is quieter and we sleep better," answers Julie.
In the end they choose the suburbs and sign the lease on Monday.
